text:
olivia: quick heads-up — I ran a manual terraform import in staging for the egress policy and now `terraform plan` wants to replace the aws_security_group and an aws_iam_role that were untouched earlier. not sure why the IDs shifted.

mike: did you run with the same provider alias? we recently added an aws.account2 alias for cross-account stuff.

olivia: ah right i imported with the default provider (no alias). the resources are defined with provider = aws.account2 in tf.

sam: that would change the resource addressing, terraform sees them as different instances. plan shows delete + create? paste the snippet.

olivia: here's the plan excerpt:
```
# module/network.aws_security_group.sg will be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_security_group" "sg" {
  ~ id = "sg-0abc123" -> (known after apply)
  + provider = aws.account2
}
```

ashley: also check state: `terraform state list | grep aws_security_group` — you might have the resource under the default provider in state.

olivia: yep it exists as `module.network.aws_security_group.sg` but state shows provider as `provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]` (no alias).

mike: easiest fix is to move the state entry to the aliased provider: `terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws:account2'` — do that in a new workspace copy and run plan.

sam: +1 for replace-provider. Alternatively re-import with `-provider=aws.account2` to create the aliased mapping.

olivia: thanks — quick q: will replace-provider keep resource IDs intact or will it force recreation?

ashley: replace-provider just remaps the provider on the state entry, it doesn't change the resource id. it should make plan no-op for provider alias mismatch. test in a safe copy first.

olivia: will do. one more wrinkle: plan also shows the aws_iam_role losing a managed_policy attachment (computed) after the import and wanting to recreate. any ideas?

mike: can be due to provider schema or newer aws provider version that changed computed attr names. what provider version do you have in the state vs in tf.lock?

olivia: state meta says provider version ~> 3.50, root module now uses 4.2.0 in lock.

sam: there you go. upgrade path changed some attribute behaviour for iam role attachments. try pinning to the old provider in that workspace or run `terraform state show module.iam.aws_iam_role.role` and compare attributes.

ashley: if it's only about policy attachments, you can `terraform import aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.example role_name:policy_arn` for the new schema or add a lifecycle ignore_changes on managed_policy_attachments until you can coordinate provider upgrades.

olivia: copying workspace now, will try replace-provider and either pin or re-import attachments. i'll report back in ~30m. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: reminder — perform state operations during off-peak window to avoid collisions (see #eng-infra rota).

mike: thanks, and if you get stuck ping me. I'll stand by for a rollback plan if replace-provider goes sideways. :eyes:

olivia: update: replace-provider worked on the copy, plan is clean for the sg now. iam attachments still flagged; will re-import those ones. thanks all.
